speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In the meantime, our hospitals will continue attending to life-threatening cases at the Emergency Departments (EDs) immediately and carry out urgent surgeries promptly.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I would just like to ask a few supplementary questions	regarding what is the main cause for the increase in hospitalisation stay from 6.1 days to seven days.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What are steps taken now to tackle that?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Can we go back to six days again?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: And lastly, how much is it due to the backlog from COVID-19 and when will this backlog clear?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are seeing more aged patients, frailer patients and patients with more co-morbidities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, the main reason that it is taking longer for them to stay in hospital is because the amount of care they need is more.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is a significant increase in the length of stay.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And that is what has fundamentally affected the strain on our capacity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have not been able to increase as much as we have previously projected because of the delays and the infrastructure upgrading and roll-out of capacity because of COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we are trying our best to catch up.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not think there is a foreseeable way in which we can go back to shorter stays because our population is getting even older.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, you will have more patients with complex healthcare needs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do have to put in quite a lot of effort to keep us as healthy as possible for as long as possible to mitigate this burden.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But once you need hospitalisation, the likelihood is that your care is likely to be more complex and longer than in the past.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: What we have to do then is to optimise the use of the capacity we do have, which is to transfer patients to step-down facilities, community facilities and also, where possible, to recover at home, so that our hospital facilities are focused on those who need that complex acute care.
